Merge all spans into one by representing all unpopulated buckets explicitly, for example: Positive bucket list: [3, 2, -5, 0, 1, -1, 3, -1] and Positive span list: [[-2, 8]] [C1][C2]. Empty spans (offset 0, length 0) are allowed and may be used to reduce the number of spans, but they are generally not useful and should be eliminated by adding their offset to the following span [C2].

Update your client libraries to use OpenMetrics 2.0 Start Timestamps by replacing the old `_created` samples with an inline Start Timestamp (st@) on the sample line itself [C2]. The OM 2.0 sample line has the following field ordering: metric_name value [timestamp] [st@start_timestamp] [# exemplar...] [C2]. Counters and histograms retain their creation semantics and support Start Timestamps; gauges do not [C2]. The OM 1.0 example used http_requests_total with the _created sample, while OM 2.0 uses http_requests_total with the st@ timestamp [C2]. The _created sample disappears entirely in OM 2.0, and the st@ timestamp appears after the value on the single CompositeValue line [C2].

Use the rate(rate(<metric_name>[<duration>])) to get the rate of the sum and the rate of the count, then divide the two rates to get the average observation size. [C2][C1]

If you have a native histogram, extract the sum and count with histogram_sum and histogram_count and divide the two rates. [C2][C1]
If you cannot avoid negative observations and are stuck with summaries or classic histograms, use two separate summaries or histograms and combine the results later with PromQL expressions. [C2]

When aggregating ratio metrics, aggregate the numerator and denominator separately and then divide the aggregated values to get the ratio [C1]. Do not take the average of a ratio or the average of an average because that is not statistically valid [C1]. If you have a Summary and want to calculate average observation size, treat it as a ratio by keeping the metric name without the _count or _sum suffix and replacing the rate with mean instead of averaging the count and sum [C1]. Always specify a without clause with the labels you are aggregating away to preserve labels like job and avoid conflicts [C1].
